simple.meaning: מֶשִׁי (meshîy) is a Hebrew object word meaning “silk (as drawn from the cocoon).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezekiel 16:10. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֶשִׁי (H4897) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מֶשִׁי (meshîy) / H4897 is traced through Ezekiel 16:10, Ezekiel 16:13 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H4897. meshi מֶ֫שִׁי noun [masculine] a costly material for garments, according to Rabb silk , (so Now Archaeology i. 124 ); whether this is based on actual tradition is dubious (etymology unknown); — absolute ׳מ Ezek 16:13 (|| שֵׁשׁ ), מֶ֑שִׁי 16:10 (|| id. ) See, further Thes Sm Da Berthol. ᵐ5 τρίχαπτα . מֻשִׁי see מוּשִׁי .

occurrences.englishText: I clothed you also with embroidered work, and put sealskin sandals on you. I dressed you with fine linen and covered you with silk.

Thus you were decked with gold and silver. Your clothing was of fine linen, silk, and embroidered work. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You were exceedingly beautiful, and you prospered to royal estate.
